name: Show timeline: a shader clip runs on its own time
description: A shader clip's TIME is its time in the clip: a paused scrub shows the same picture every time and holds still, playback carries on from it, and an export renders the same moments. The shader's brightness is TIME / 4, so the output says which moment it is. Before the clip the layer shows its own white (an export refuses a blank first frame).

steps.label: A 20 s time-ramp shader clip at 2 s, in point 1 s
Paused at 7 s: the clip is 6 s in (brightness 0.5)
Still 6 s in after a second and a half: a paused shader holds
Scrub back to 4.2 s: 3.2 s in (0.8)
Playing: the picture follows the playhead

eval.true.js: (async () => { const s = await __show.snapshot(); const t = __show.show().currentTime; const got = (s.mean_rgba[0] + s.mean_rgba[1] + s.mean_rgba[2]) / 3; const want = ((t - 1) / 4) % 1; return Math.abs(got - want) < 0.06 ? { got: +got.toFixed(3), want: +want.toFixed(3), t: +t.toFixed(2) } : false; })()
eval.true.label: brightness matches the clip time

steps.label: Paused again: still on the playhead
